summary: Short demo of Redwood Optimize/Console features focused on prompt guardrails, A/B compare, and regression alerts for a planned pilot. Customer cares about drift detection thresholds, explainability of alerts, and SSO + KMS for Private.

Security: SSO, SOC2, KMS, data residency
transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan: Alright good afternoon everyone, uh thanks for taking the time. This is Jordan from Redwood Inference, I'm the customer's AE for this account. With me is Maya Chen, our solutions engineer. Maya, say hi.
[00:00:12] Maya: Hey team, hi everyone. I'll be doing most of the demo parts, I'll jump into the console and show the prompt sets and the regression alerts.
[00:00:19] Priya (Bluefin): Thanks — excited. Quick context, we're evaluating quality monitoring for our summarization and extraction flows. We need early warn for regression and a way to run A/B comparisons across fine-tuned variants.
[00:00:33] Ethan (Bluefin): And from infra side we need to understand data residency and KMS integration — we do not want any plaintext logs leaving the VPC.
[00:00:42] Jordan: Totally. High-level agenda is: Maya will do a sandbox walkthrough in the Console, show prompt-set upload, run an A/B compare, then show regression alerting and how those alerts surface in the API and the Console. We'll finish with runbook/next steps.
[00:01:02] Maya: Ok jumping in. I'm in the Redwood Console — top-left you can see the 'Evals' tab, then 'Prompt sets'. I have a sample set called 'bluefin-summ-guards-v1' loaded. Note the file shape is CSV with question, reference, and metadata columns, we can accept JSONL too.
[00:01:21] [00:01:21] Maya: There's a quick preview; transcription from the meeting shows some words slightly off; in the console we map tokenized responses and we do pairwise scoring by default.
[00:01:35] Priya: Quick Q — can we attach business logic labels? Like 'PII-invoked' or 'hallucination-severity'? We need structured labels for downstream routing.
[00:01:44] Maya: Yes — the prompt set schema supports arbitrary label columns. You can configure a custom rubric — we've seen customers use 'safety_flag', 'coref_errors', etc. Those become fields in the alert payload.
[00:01:59] Ethan: How heavy is scoring? If we run nightly—say 100k prompts—how does cost look?
[00:02:07] Maya: Two parts: model compute cost which is per-token, and then eval compute which is lightweight; if you use pairwise or model-based metrics that runs LLM eval calls, that's heavier. Optimize suggests batching + a cheaper metric per recency window and a heavier run weekly.
[00:02:24] [00:02:24] Jordan: Also mention dedicated vs hosted — if you need predictable unit costs for 100k/day inference, dedicated capacity gives fixed throughput and predictable pricing.
[00:02:35] Priya: Could you show the A/B compare now — how do you ensure statistical significance?
[00:02:41] Maya: Sure. I'm creating an A/B compare run between 'gptx-small-2026-tuned' and 'gptx-quant-8bit' — Console has built-in significance tests (bootstrap CIs) and you can choose metrics. For extractive tasks we use F1 and token-level overlap; for summarization we show ROUGE variants plus a pairwise preference metric we call 'pref score'.
[00:03:05] Maya: I'm kicking off the job. You'll see sample-size estimation up-front — we estimate ~2000 pairs to reach 95% confidence for a delta of 0.02 on pref score.
[00:03:20] Priya: That's helpful. For regulatory audit we need the audit trail — who ran the eval and the model versions.
[00:03:27] Maya: All runs are versioned. We store model sigs, quantization profile, and the exact prompt set snapshot. Audit log entries are exportable for your compliance team. You can also set retention policies on the Console.
[00:03:39] Ethan: On the Private deployment side — KMS integration — can Redwood call our KMS in the VPC, or do keys have to be in Redwood's HSM?
[00:03:48] Jordan: Both patterns supported. For hosted API customers we support customer-managed keys via a KMS federation pattern; for Private we can do in-VPC KMS/HSM integrations. We'll follow up with our security engineering docs.
[00:03:59] [00:03:59] Priya: Are regression alerts explainable? We want to know why the alert fired — e.g., which prompts trended down and what metric changed.
[00:04:07] Maya: Yes. Alerts include a breakdown: metric deltas, sample slices (by metadata), and example pairs that regressed. We also provide an 'explain' view — a short diff of model outputs and an attribution highlight for key tokens.
[00:04:20] Priya: Nice, can we route those alerts into our Slack and JIRA?
[00:04:24] Maya: Yep — webhooks, Slack, and JIRA integration exist. You can customize thresholds per channel and per team.
[00:04:31] Ethan: Any false-positive tuning? We don't want noisy alerts.
[00:04:35] Maya: You can set a cooldown window, require multiple consecutive windows to trigger, and add a weight to metrics so less important metrics don't noisily flip.
[00:04:44] [00:04:44] Jordan: We also recommend a two-tiered policy: P0 alerts to on-call, P1 to a monitoring channel, and P2 as weekly digest — Console policies support that.
[00:04:56] Priya: Show a regression alert history?
[00:05:00] Maya: Opening the 'Regression' tab. Here's a recent alert — it shows pref score drop -0.045, affected slice 'docs-length>2000', and 12 example pairs attached. The transcription will show some occasional word swaps — in the example you can see some OCR errors; we surface original token offsets so you can cross-check.
[00:05:20] Priya: Can the alert run a canary rollback automatically?
[00:05:24] Maya: Yes, if you integrate with the Redwood routing policy you can configure automatic fallback to a safe model variant and then initiate a rollback run. We support canary durations and max-fallback-rate.
[00:05:35] Ethan: For our PoC we'd like to test with VPC/private infra. Any constraints on embeddings or other features?
[00:05:42] Jordan: Embeddings are supported on Private; some accelerator optimizations vary by hardware. We'll need to map model choices to your GPU types — Maya can run a korte compatibility check during the pilot.
[00:05:55] Maya: Quick demo of the API flow — you can upload a prompt set via /v1/evals/upload, then create a run via /v1/evals/runs with parameters: metric list, baseline model, alt model ids, and slice configs. The API returns run_id and a polling endpoint for status.
[00:06:15] Priya: Any limits? Throttling?
[00:06:19] Maya: Default rate limits apply in the hosted tier but for pilot/Dedicated we can bump them. The Console also allows long-running jobs to be scheduled and handled via background workers so you won't hit per-second throttles for large batch evals.
[00:06:31] Priya: Security question — soc2 type II and data handling for eval inputs — does Redwood persist prompt text?
[00:06:38] Jordan: By default we persist for 30 days for debugging; you can set a zero-retention policy or opt-in to encrypted-at-rest with your KMS and restrict access via RBAC. We're SOC 2 Type II in our hosted operations and provide attestations for enterprise engagements.
[00:06:52] Ethan: Good. About the A/B compare output — can we export the per-prompt diffs as a CSV so our analysts can run custom stats?
[00:06:59] Maya: Yes — exportable CSV/JSONL with per-prompt metrics, model outputs, token usage. We also provide a prebuilt Jupyter notebook for quick exploration.
[00:07:10] [00:07:10] Priya: What about golden labeling — we want to keep human labels in our system. Is there an import/export pattern?
[00:07:16] Maya: You can import human labels as a column; after runs you can mark adjudicated labels and re-run comparisons. Also support for third-party labeling tools via webhook or S3 exchange.
[00:07:28] Priya: If an eval shows a hallucination spike, can the alert optionally include a suggested rollback and a remediation checklist?
[00:07:37] Maya: Yes — the alert template can include an automated remediation playbook: rollbacks, recommended prompt templates, and suggested quantization/temperature changes.
[00:07:46] [00:07:46] Ethan: Tell me more about the metrics — pairwise vs model-eval metrics — which are more reliable?
[00:07:51] Maya: Pairwise preference (human-like) is usually more aligned with user preference but requires more compute or annotated data. Model-based metrics are cheaper and can be calibrated: Optimize provides calibration tools and probes to align model-based metrics to human judgements.
[00:08:07] Jordan: Also important — prefix caching and KV cache mismatches can cause tail-latency differences which sneak into evals. We recommend evaluating with the same runtime config you use in production so evals match behavior.
[00:08:21] Priya: Anything else on the Console before we move to questions?
[00:08:25] Maya: One last thing — we have a 'regression heatmap' view that shows metric drift over calendar windows and correlated metadata slices; it's useful for root cause.
[00:08:37] [00:08:37] Priya: Ok good — quick round of questions from our data team — Lina?
[00:08:42] Lina (Bluefin): Hi. Two things: 1) for prompt templating across languages — we use multi-lingual content — does the pref metric behave cross-lingually? 2) CI integration for our test suite.
[00:08:54] Maya: For multi-lingual, you can segment by language slice — the model-based metrics need per-language calibration. We also support embedding-based similarity metrics which generalize better. For CI, you can run evals as part of your pipeline via API and fail builds on regressions.
[00:09:10] Lina: For embeddings similarity, do you recommend cosine thresholds or learned thresholds?
[00:09:15] Maya: Start with cosine + a language-aware threshold, then run a small annotated calibration set to pick a threshold. Optimize can suggest thresholds automatically based on your seed labels.
[00:09:25] [00:09:25] Jordan: Ok we're nearing the 10 minute mark in our notes but we have another 40 minutes — open floor for deeper tech — Ethan wants to talk infra.
[00:09:36] Ethan: Yeah I want an architecture sketch for Private — how much of the control plane remains in Redwood vs in the customer's VPC?
[00:09:44] Maya: Control plane services (UI, billing, and marketplace) can be run as a customer-managed instance or via Redwood-hosted control plane that talks over a narrow control channel. Data plane (model host, KV cache) runs in your VPC. For air-gapped we have an on-prem bundle.
[00:10:00] Ethan: Is there any telemetry that leaves the VPC by default? For security we need minimal external calls.
[00:10:06] Jordan: Minimal telemetry can be configured; you can set egress rules. For audits, you can opt into logs we ship or keep all logs in your S3 bucket.
[00:10:16] Priya: About the pilot — what's a typical PoC scope you suggest?
[00:10:20] Maya: Typical: 1) 500-2,000 annotated prompts, 2) run nightly regressions for two weeks, 3) one A/B compare and an integration with one alerting channel. We often do a 4-week pilot to cover edge cases.
[00:10:34] Jordan: I'll put a suggested pilot plan in the follow-up email along with pricing bands and security docs.
[00:10:40] [00:10:40] Priya: Great. Quick objection — we use Vertex for some eval workloads; why Redwood for monitoring?
[00:10:47] Jordan: Good Q. Redwood focuses on inference-first metrics and production observability: automatic KV/prefix cache-aware evals, built-in fallback routing, and cost-aware suggestions. Also the unified experience across hosted/dedicated/private is key for operational teams.
[00:11:02] Priya: That helps, thank you.
... (transcript continues with intermittent timestamps and deeper technical discussion) ...
[00:25:17] Maya: Showing the alert config UI — you can create an alert with multiple metric triggers and a slice expression. Here's a slice for 'country in [CN, RU]' and 'docs-length > 1000'. UI warns on small-sample sizes.
[00:30:02] Priya: Can the alert correlate to user metrics like NPS drop or support ticket spikes?
[00:30:09] Maya: You can ingest external signals via webhooks and correlate them in the heatmap. We also have a prebuilt connector to major ticketing systems.
[00:36:15] Ethan: For the A/B runner, what about seeding randomness? We need reproducible runs.
[00:36:22] Maya: Runs can be seeded and all randomness fixed; the run snapshot records seed and model environment. We also version prompt canonicalization steps.
[00:41:10] Priya: Let's talk about explainability — can we get token-level attributions for why model B beats model A on a prompt?
[00:41:18] Maya: We provide a token-diff view plus simple attention-based heuristics and a small annotation UI to mark which tokens matter. For deeper attribution we can export logits if you run in Private.
[00:46:00] Jordan: Time check — last 7 minutes, let's do a recap and next steps.
[00:46:10] Maya: Recap: 1) Console demo — prompt sets, A/B compare, regression alerts + explainability; 2) API flow for evals and exports; 3) Security - SSO/SAML, SOC2, KMS, retention controls; 4) Pilot proposal.
[00:46:30] Jordan: Next steps: we'll share the pilot plan and pricing, Maya will run the A/B benchmark on your sample set, and we'll send the security pack. Any blockers?
[00:46:40] Priya: No blockers; we'll assemble sample prompts and share credentials for a staging environment.
[00:46:47] Ethan: We'll review security docs once received and schedule an infra sync.
[00:46:52] Priya: Great thanks everyone.
[00:46:55] Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up. End of recording.

[00:53:00] End of meeting (approx).
